nodes.name: LDH-WO₄²⁻ preparation
nodes.procedure: A nanohybrid of WO₄²⁻ intercalated Mg-Al LDHs, denoted as LDH-WO₄²⁻, was first prepared via a structure-reconstruction route by dispersing a Mg-Al layered double oxide (LDO) in Na₂WO₄ aqueous solution.
nodes.source_text: A nanohybrid of WO₄²⁻ intercalated Mg-Al LDHs, denoted as LDH-WO₄²⁻, was first prepared via a structure-reconstruction route by dispersing a Mg-Al layered double oxide (LDO) in Na₂WO₄ aqueous solution.

nodes.name: Calcination to LDO-WO₃
nodes.procedure: The LDH-WO₄²⁻ was then calcined at 500°C for 2h leading to the in situ formation of ultrathin 2D WO₃ within the interlayer 2D space of LDHs, resulting in an alternative stacking composite of ultrathin WO₃ layers and LDO layers, denoted as LDO-WO₃.

nodes.name: Acid dissolution to ML-WO₃·H₂O
nodes.procedure: By acid-dissolving the host LDO layers of LDO-WO₃, ML-WO₃·H₂O NSs were obtained after water-washing and vacuum-drying.

nodes.name: PtCl₆²⁻ adsorption
nodes.procedure: The so-obtained ML-WO₃·H₂O NSs were dispersed in an H₂PtCl₆ aqueous solution, leading to the adsorption of PtCl₆²⁻ ions on ML-WO₃·H₂O NSs, producing PtCl₆²⁻/ML-WO₃·H₂O.
nodes.source_text: The so-obtained ML-WO₃·H₂O NSs were dispersed in an H₂PtCl₆ aqueous solution, leading to the adsorption of PtCl₆²⁻ ions...

nodes.name: Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ annealing
nodes.procedure: The PtCl₆²⁻/ML-WO₃·H₂O was then annealed under a reductive Ar-H₂ atmosphere at 300°C for 1h, gaining Pt-SA/ML-WO₃.

nodes.source_text: The electrocatalytic HER activity of the Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ was evaluated in an N₂ saturated 0.5 M H₂SO₄ solution using a standard three-electrode system with a scan rate of 2 mV s⁻¹ at room temperature. Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ coated on glassy carbon (GC) was used as the working electrode, a graphite rod as the counter electrode, and an Ag/AgCl electrode as the reference electrode. All the potentials were referenced to a reverse hydrogen electrode (RHE). ... The onset overpotential, η_os and the overpotential to drive a current density (j) of -10 mA cm⁻² η₁₀, of Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ are ≈ 0 and -22 mV, respectively ... overpotential to drive a high j of -100 mA cm⁻² for Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ is ≈ -50 mV ... Tafel slope of Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ ... ≈ 27 mV dec⁻¹ ... mass activity of Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ (≈ 87 A mgPt⁻¹) at -50 mV ... TOF of Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ at -50 mV is up to ≈ 87 H₂ s⁻¹ site⁻¹ ... C_dl value of Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ (≈ 36.38 mF cm⁻²) ... R_ct value of Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ (≈ 10.7 Ω) ... No obvious change was observed for its polarization curves before and after 10 000 CV cycles ... multi-current chronopotentiometry (CP) curves determined at constant j ranging from -50 to -200 mA cm⁻² for total 150 h ... chronoamperometric curve at a constant η of -50 mV (≈ -30 mA cm⁻¹) for 60 h ... ≈ 100% Faradaic yield

nodes.description: Long-term stability on carbon cloth in H-type cell
nodes.source_text: the long-term durability of Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ deposed on carbon clothes (CC) for electrocatalytic HER was determined using an H-type electrochemical cell. No obvious loss of activity is also observed on the multi-current chronopotentiometry (CP) curves determined at constant j ranging from -50 to -200 mA cm⁻² for total 150 h ... chronoamperometric curve at a constant η of -50 mV (≈ -30 mA cm⁻¹) for 60 h

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt content of Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ determined to be ≈0.20 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt content of Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ was determined using ICP-OES to be ≈0.20 wt%, indicating that Pt species are successfully immobilized on ML-WO₃.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ and ML-WO₃ exhibit cubic WO₃ phase (JCPDS No. 41-0905); ML-WO₃·H₂O shows orthorhombic WO₃·H₂O phase (JCPDS No. 84-0886). No impurities detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1, the Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ and ML-WO₃ exhibit the same XRD patterns that match well with the standard patterns of cubic WO₃ (JCPDS No. 41-0905).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ shows irregular flaky morphology similar to ML-WO₃·H₂O and ML-WO₃, different from stone-like bulk WO₃. No serious sintering observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images (Figure 2a-c) indicate that the Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ has an irregular flaky morphology, similar to those of ML-WO₃·H₂O and ML-WO₃.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt atoms observed as separate brighter dots at W vacancy positions with lattice spacing 0.371 nm (100) cubic WO₃. No Pt aggregates detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, many separate and brighter dots can be observed (as marked using yellow circles), which are attributed to Pt atoms (Figure 5a).

nodes.characterization_summary: Average thicknesses: ML-WO₃·H₂O ≈1.5 nm, ML-WO₃ ≈0.9 nm, Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ ≈1.0 nm, all corresponding to monolayer thickness. Monolayer ratios >93%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The average thicknesses of ML-WO₃·H₂O, ML-WO₃, and Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ NSs were estimated using AFM (Figure 3a-c) to be ≈1.5, 0.9, and 1.0 nm, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: All samples show O-H stretching at 3415 cm⁻¹ and water deformation at 1623 cm⁻¹. ML-WO₃·H₂O: W=O at 959 cm⁻¹, W-O at 649 cm⁻¹. ML-WO₃ and Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ show shifts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: All of FT-IR spectra (Figure 4a) show a broad band around 3415 cm⁻¹ and a peak at 1623 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: ML-WO₃·H₂O shows orthorhombic WO₃·H₂O peaks at 192, 647, 946 cm⁻¹. ML-WO₃ and Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ show cubic WO₃ peaks at 266, 697, 801 cm⁻¹. No Pt signals detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra of ML-WO₃·H₂O and ML-WO₃ (Figure 4b) exhibit the characteristic signals of orthorhombic WO₃·H₂O and cubic WO₃ respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ shows W 4f peaks at 37.40/35.20 eV (W⁶⁺/W⁵⁺, 10% W⁵⁺), O 1s at 530.12 eV, Pt 4f at 74.70/71.38 eV (Pt⁰/Pt²⁺, 28% Pt²⁺), O/W=2.66. Peaks shift lower by 0.3 eV vs ML-WO₃ indicating electron transfer from Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ the peaks of W 4f₅/₂ and 4f₇/₂ appear at 37.40 and 35.20 eV, respectively... The R_at of W⁵⁺ species in the total W is estimated to be ≈10% and those of lattice O²⁻, H-OH, and W-OH species in the total O to be ≈61% 14% and 25% (Table S1, Supporting Information), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Symmetric EPR signal at g=2.0032 confirms O vacancies. Signal intensity increases: ML-WO₃·H₂O < ML-WO₃ < Pt-SA/ML-WO₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A symmetric EPR signal at g = 2.0032 is observed for ML-WO₃·H₂O ML-WO₃ and Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ (Figure S9, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Type-IV isotherm with H3 hysteresis. S_BET: 86.4, 90.3, 98.2 m²/g; V_p: 0.28, 0.31, 0.35 cm³/g; d_p: 13, 14, 10 nm for ML-WO₃·H₂O, ML-WO₃, Pt-SA/ML-WO₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The N₂ adsorption-desorption tests were performed... The BET specific surface areas (S_BET) and average pore volumes (V_p) of ML-WO₃·H₂O (≈86.4 m² g⁻¹ and 0.28 cm³ g⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: C_dl = 36.38 mF cm⁻² for Pt-SA/ML-WO₃, higher than ML-WO₃·H₂O (6.23 mF cm⁻²), ML-WO₃ (8.01 mF cm⁻²), and 20 wt% Pt/C (5.18 mF cm⁻²), indicating larger ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C_dl value of Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ (≈36.38 mF cm⁻²) is obviously higher than those of 20 wt% Pt/C (≈5.18 mF cm⁻²), ML-WO₃·H₂O (≈6.23 mF cm⁻²), and ML-WO₃ (≈8.01 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: R_ct = 10.7 Ω for Pt-SA/ML-WO₃, lower than ML-WO₃·H₂O (>5000 Ω), ML-WO₃ (418 Ω), and 20 wt% Pt/C (44.1 Ω), indicating fast charge transfer kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The analysis results (Table S5, Supporting Information) show that the R_ct value of Pt-SA/ML-WO₃ (≈10.7 Ω) is much lower than those of ML-WO₃·H₂O (>5000 Ω) and ML-WO₃ (≈418 Ω), and even lower than that of 20 wt% Pt/C (≈44.1 Ω).
